Máté Marjai

Engineering leader with 18+ years in payments and product-led B2B SaaS. At Primer I lead two teams in the Orchestration org, one through an Engineering Manager who reports to me. At peak the org had 15 engineers, including Staff Engineers, Tech Leads and an EM, across iOS, Android, Web and backend. I grew a Senior Engineer into the company's only home-grown EM in over two years, and built engineering-wide mechanisms that other teams adopted, from AI-assisted engineering to testing standards and incident fire drills. Before Primer I was a seed-stage CTO twice: I co-founded BonsaiX and raised a $500k seed round, and led Popdeem's pivot from a consumer app to a revenue-generating B2B platform. Earlier, a founding engineer of SumUp's Dublin team (0 to 15 engineers).

Engineering Manager, Orchestration (Conversion & Payment Operations) at Primer

Feb 2024 - Present

Key Achievements

Series C payments platform. I lead two teams. Conversion owns the merchant checkout SDKs on iOS, Android and Web, and I run it through an Engineering Manager who reports to me. Payment Operations owns payment state, timeline and search services, and I lead it directly. At peak the org I led had 15 engineers, including Staff Engineers, Tech Leads and an Engineering Manager.

  • Org design: designed the split of Experience into Conversion and a net-new Payment Operations team, held the design through exec review, then hired the Conversion EM and handed the team over to him within four weeks. Introduced a delegated Tech Lead model that other teams adopted.
  • Engineering strategy: own the 2027 vision for Payment Operations and wrote the 2027 headcount plan for both teams. Set and drove the team's developer experience goal (local development, flaky tests, CI speed), which took it to industry P90 on developer experience scores.
  • Growing leaders: grew a Senior Engineer into an EM over 18 months, wrote the ramp-up and Associate EM path the org now uses, grew another engineer to Staff, turned an underperformer into the Android lead, and took two engineers through promotion. Rewrote the EM job spec and redesigned the frontend hiring challenge.
  • Business impact: led the Checkout SDK rearchitecture, cutting merchant integration time from weeks to hours. Found that a top merchant's 9-second checkout load time was an outlier and drove the fix (median 2.2s to 0.3s, P95 3.9s to 1.8s; platform median now under 400ms). Their move to the new checkout delivered a 1.17% conversion uplift.
  • AI-first engineering: made AI-assisted development the team's default and spread it across engineering. Rolled out AI code review on SDK and backend repos for all engineers, built an AI on-call assistant adopted by two other teams, added AI ticket-quality scoring for maintenance work, and shipped an AI interview-evaluation tool, calibrated to the competency matrix, to every EM. Delivered localisation into 22 languages with AI for about $3.6k less than the alternative.
  • Standards and operational readiness: authored the company's engineering testing standard, including the scorecard model for client-side services that other teams adopted. Created incident fire drills, which other EMs now run from my framework. Wrote the backend on-call guidance and split the on-call rota across teams.
  • Exec and merchant escalations: represented engineering in high-stakes merchant escalations alongside the exec team. I reframed headline claims with data, established the real root cause so commercial decisions rested on facts, and kept urgent demands inside the normal escalation process so no single merchant could set the priorities for everyone else.
  • Service health and observability: introduced numeric baselines for the systems I own: dedicated health dashboards, service scorecards (Payment Operations services just under 80/100) and a fortnightly monitoring review. Unified client analytics with Datadog so a single payment can be traced end to end. Cut the escalation backlog from 100+ tickets to a 1–2 week steady state, and made an infrastructure tier decision worth about $24k a year.
  • Culture: no regretted attrition over 16 months and 9+/10 on manager impact in the culture survey. Rebooted the engineering blog and wrote its first article.
